title: Benin Palace Plaque
craftSpec: Pigments hand-ground in linseed or walnut oil over sized and primed support; layered from dark underpainting (imprimatura) to opaque highlights.
region: Nigeria (Royal Palace of the Oba, Benin City, Edo State)
note: Hundreds of rectangular plaques like this one hung on the pillars of the royal palace in Benin City, fixed by nails punched through them. They were cast by the lost-wax method, in brass that came partly from bracelet-shaped ingots bought from Portuguese traders. British forces took them when they sacked the city in 1897, and the Foreign Office gave a large number to the British Museum. From 1950 the museum sold more than 30 to the Nigerian government as duplicates; the sales stopped in 1972.

seeText: Brass relief plaque of a standing figure in a tall beaded crown and collar, holding objects, the background decorated with flower-like rosettes and nail holes. Feel: regal, ceremonial, solid, historic.
